problem_type: data URL parser rejects standard media-type parameters
symptom: Opening a project whose canvas nodes carry an inline `data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<percent-encoded>` thumbnail failed hydration: parseDataUrl threw "Invalid data URL", the error escaped the nomi:projects:read-async IPC handler, and the workbench showed "项目暂时无法打开" instead of the canvas. It surfaced as the E2E-Linux selection-toolbar walk red.
direct_cause: parseDataUrl matched only an optional `;base64` parameter before the comma (/^data:([^;,]+)?(;base64)?,.../). A media type carrying any other RFC 2397 parameter — `;utf8`, `;charset=utf-8` — did not match, so the function threw before the embedded-media localizer could slim the URL.
class_root: The single shared data-URL decoder used by every embedded-media and asset ingestion path did not implement the RFC 2397 media-type parameter grammar; it recognized exactly one parameter (`;base64`) and treated every other well-formed data URL as invalid, so any caller that received a parameterized non-base64 data URL failed identically.
affected_population: Users whose projects contain inline SVG or text data URLs written as data:<mime>;utf8,... or data:<mime>;charset=...,... (common for seeded or hand-authored thumbnails)
Users opening older or externally-authored projects that embed such data URLs, which now route through the M1 cutover embedded-media localization on hydrate
Any asset, audio, or generation-output ingestion path that decodes a parameterized non-base64 data URL through the shared parseDataUrl
entry_points: localizeEmbeddedDataUrl via localizeEmbeddedMediaUrls during workspace manifest read/slimming

external_sources.purpose: Confirm the data URL grammar is data:[<mediatype>][;base64],<data> where <mediatype> may include one or more `;parameter=value` segments, and only a `;base64` token selects base64 decoding.
Confirm non-base64 data payloads are percent-encoded text (charset/utf8 parameters are permitted) and are decoded by URL-decoding the data portion.

invariants: parseDataUrl accepts any RFC 2397 data URL whose media type carries zero or more parameters, and selects base64 decoding only when a `;base64` parameter is present.
A non-base64 payload is percent-decoded; a payload that is not valid percent-encoding is preserved verbatim rather than throwing.
Every embedded-media and asset ingestion path decodes data URLs through this one shared decoder, so a parameterized non-base64 data URL never aborts hydration, slimming, or asset capture.
generality_proof: A repository-wide search for parseDataUrl callers converges on the single decoder in electron/assets/assetBytes.ts (workspaceManifest, audioTaskRunner, projectAssetStore, generationOutputMaterializer). Fixing the grammar at that shared boundary repairs every caller at once; the added unit test enumerates the base64, `;utf8`, `;charset`, bare, default-media-type, malformed-percent, and non-data-URL cases so the boundary contract is pinned for all consumers.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Decode any RFC 2397 data URL into bytes plus content type for every embedded-media and asset ingestion caller.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: localizeEmbeddedDataUrl via parseDataUrl during manifest read/slimming
same_class_entry_points.evidence: The failing hydrate path decodes the inline SVG data URL through the shared parseDataUrl; with the parameter grammar fixed the selection-toolbar project opens to the canvas instead of the repair dialog.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: parseDataUrl at audioTaskRunner.ts inline audio ingestion
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Audio ingestion calls the same shared decoder, so a data:audio/...;charset payload now decodes through the same corrected grammar rather than throwing.
Asset persistence localizes data URLs via the shared decoder and inherits the fix for parameterized non-base64 inputs.
Generation output capture decodes returned data URLs through the same boundary and inherits the corrected parameter handling.

recurrence.reason: Every current and future embedded-media or asset path decodes data URLs through this single function; any parameterized non-base64 data URL from real project data, generated output, or imported assets would reproduce the throw at every one of these call sites.
same_class_scan: Searched electron/ and src/ for parseDataUrl and confirmed all consumers import the one decoder in electron/assets/assetBytes.ts.
Confirmed electron/catalog/assetValueScheme.ts uses its own parseDataUrlHeader (a separate parser) and is out of this boundary's scope.
Checked the workspace-manifest slimming, audio ingestion, project-asset persistence, and generation-output capture call sites independently.

prevention.invariant: The shared data-URL decoder implements the full RFC 2397 media-type parameter grammar and base64 selection, so no caller re-implements or bypasses data-URL parsing.
prevention.failure_mode: A data URL with any parameter run parses to the correct bytes and content type; only a genuinely malformed data URL throws, and a non-percent-encoded payload is preserved verbatim. Regression tests fail if the `;utf8`/`;charset` forms ever regress to throwing.
prevention.strategy: Match the entire parameter run up to the comma, detect base64 by the presence of a `;base64` token, percent-decode otherwise with a verbatim fallback, and pin the grammar with an enumerated unit test at the shared boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: The shared decoder was corrected in place; there is no parallel legacy data-URL parser to remove. electron/catalog/assetValueScheme.ts keeps its own header parser by design and is unaffected.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The defect is in Nomi's own data-URL decoding, not in a third-party package version; RFC 2397 is a stable standard, not a dependency to upgrade.

migration: No stored data is rewritten. Projects whose payloads already contain parameterized non-base64 data URLs now hydrate: the same embedded-media localization runs, decoding those URLs into localized asset files on read exactly as base64 URLs already were.
residual_risks: Payloads declared as non-base64 that are neither valid percent-encoding nor plain text are stored as their raw bytes rather than rejected, mirroring prior lenient behavior for base64-less data URLs.
electron/catalog/assetValueScheme.ts intentionally retains a separate header parser; a future consolidation onto parseDataUrl would need its own contract.
